title: stability-as-a-product-sprint-proposal-and-onboarding-draft
content:
Overview:

This is a working proposal to treat reliability as a product ("stability-as-a-product") and to run a 6-week cross-functional sprint to ship baseline SLOs, a minimal operator playbook, and an onboarding path for service owners. The goal is not to finish every SLO for the whole fleet; it is to create repeatable patterns, templates, and a lightweight cadence that teams can adopt quickly.

Purpose and success criteria:
- Establish a repeatable SLO onboarding flow (template + step-by-step checklist) that service teams can complete within 2 weeks.
- Deploy SLI collection and dashboards for 6 pilot services by end of Sprint 3.
- Run two error-budget experiments (one conservative threshold, one aggressive) and capture outcomes.
- Reduce mean time to detect (MTTD) for pilot services by 30% from baseline.
- Produce a short, shareable "stability kit" (doc + 1 pager + dashboard template).

Scope (what we will do in this run):
- Define SLO taxonomy and guardrails (availability, latency P95/P99, end-to-end user errors).
- Build a one-click dashboard template in Grafana and an exportable KPI CSV.
- Create onboarding playbook: stakeholders, required telemetry, monitoring checks, runbook snippets.
- Instrument 6 pilot services (mix of hosted-api, dedicated, and internal infra).
- Prepare a comms plan and training session for service owners.

Out of scope for this sprint:
- Fleet-wide retrofitting of legacy services requiring deep refactor.
- Long-term tooling investments (e.g., rewriting our metrics ingestion) — we will instead use current telemetry with clear migration path.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Project lead (PM): Priya Kapoor — overall program progress, GTM of stability kit to org.
- SRE product owner: Avery Chen — SLI/SLO definition, runbooks, measurement.
- Metrics/Telemetry lead: Ethan Morales — dashboards, instrumentation, alert rules.
- Console/UX contact: Lina Park — dashboard UX and onboarding modal.
- Solutions Eng liaison: Noah Thompson — pilot service onboarding and customer-facing docs.
- Executive sponsor: Marta Silva — organizational unblock, exec comms.

Pilot service candidates (initial):
- hosted-generation-api (low-latency critical)
- embeddings-batch-worker (throughput, cost-sensitive)
- dedicated-queue-gateway (tenant isolation path)
- internal-cache-proxy (infra dependency)
- feature-store-indexer (periodic job)
- rollout-edge-router (ingress path)

High-level timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0: Kickoff, merchant-of-signal discovery with pilot leads, finalize SLO taxonomy.
- Week 1: Implement basic SLI collection (latency, errors, success rate) for first two pilots; draft dashboards.
- Week 2: Dashboard templates usable; onboarding checklist published; training 1 for pilot owners.
- Week 3: Instrument next two pilots; run first error-budget experiment on pilot A.
- Week 4: Iterate alerts and runbooks based on experiment; prepare public notes and lessons.
- Week 5: Instrument remaining pilots; run second error-budget experiment on pilot B; finalize kit.
- Week 6: Retro, org training drop, and rollout schedule for next cohort.

Sprint lanes and explicit deliverables (per sprint):
- Telemetry lane (Ethan): SLI exporters, tag conventions, dashboard JSON.
- Playbook lane (Avery): SLO template, runbook snippets, incident flow.
- Onboarding lane (Noah + Lina): playbook UI modal, training slides, office hours schedule.
- Measurement lane (Priya): baselines, success metrics, error-budget experiment plan.

Example SLO template (compressed):
- SLO name: "user-facing-generate-success-rate"
- SLI: fraction of requests with final status == 200 and latency < 800ms measured at request ingress.
- SLO target: 99.5% rolling 30d with a 7-day error budget.
- Alerting: page on 99.0% 1d, warn on 99.3% 3d.
- Runbook snippet: check upstream model availability, check GPU pool saturation, escalate to dedicated-fallback route.

Communication and adoption plan:
- Week 0: Slack announcement in #eng-org + invite to kickoff.
- Week 2: Lunch-and-learn + recording + workshop sign-up for 1:1 onboarding.
- Persistent: office hours twice per week during sprints.
- Post-sprint: quarterly "stability showcase" where pilot teams present outcomes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Pilot teams lack capacity to instrument telemetry.
  Mitigation: provide a short instrumentation bundle (scripts + sample metrics) and hands-on pairing.
- Risk: Too many dashboards with inconsistent labels.
  Mitigation: enforce tag and metric naming conventions; provide a linting script.
- Risk: Alert fatigue from aggressive thresholds.
  Mitigation: start with conservative thresholds and ramp; include alert snooze workflow.

Operational playbook highlights (to land quickly):
- Lightweight incident classifier: user-impacting vs non-user impacting.
- Escalation ladder: service owner -> SRE on-call -> platform-blitz -> exec notify only after sustained error budget burn > 50% in 24h.
- Runbook template fields: symptom, immediate checks, probable causes, remediation steps, rollback options, post-incident actions.

Metrics to track (dashboard):
- SLO attainment (rolling 7d/30d) per pilot service.
- Error budget remaining (days) and burn rate.
- MTTD and MTTR per pilot.
- Number of alerts per service and alerts suppressed.
- Instrumentation completion percent (how many services have required SLIs).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who will own long-term enforcement and policy (knit into dev onboarding)? @Marta to propose org owner.
- Decide default SLO window and error budget policy across product vs infra.
- Do we expose customer-facing SLOs publicly for hosted-api? Legal + product input required.
- Readme for metric naming conventions (reference to metrics registry) needs update.

Quick kickoff checklist (first 72 hours):
- [ ] Confirm pilot list and contact leads.
- [ ] Run initial telemetry health check for each pilot.
- [ ] Create sprint JIRA epic and link to CONFLUENCE:STAB-PROD-2026.
- [ ] Post kickoff notes and invite to training.

Notes to self (working thoughts):
- Keep first kit intentionally minimal — frictionless wins adoption.
- Use existing dashboard tech (Grafana) to show concrete value; avoid building new control plane this run.
- Capture one clear story per pilot (e.g., how we caught a regression using the new SLO) to show post-sprint.

Appendix: useful links and references:
- Confluence: /display/STAB/Stability+Productization+Overview (CONFLUENCE:STAB-PROD-2026)
- Jira epic: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INFRA-4721
- Slack channel: #stability-guild

End of draft.

-- Avery (SRE PO)
